newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi's former dictator Banda quits politics.
newsitem.headline: Malawi's former dictator Banda quits politics.

text.p: Malawi's former president and dictator for nearly 30 years, Kamuzu Banda, has told his party he wants to quit politics and retire as its life president.
Banda told the main opposition Malawi Congress Party's (MCP) annual convention that he wanted to step aside to let younger politicians take over.
"For my part, the time has come to take stock of Malawi's achievements and my role in the country's development," he said in a letter.
"It is therefore appropriate for me to stand aside from party matters and to encourage a new generation to come forward and serve both the party and the country" Banda wrote.
Banda's grip on Malawi slipped when he lost the presidency to a former protege Bakili Muluzi in the country's first democratic elections in 1994.
He was prime minister when Malawi gained independence from Britain in 1964, became president in 1966 and proclaimed himself president for life in 1971, crushing dissent.

Officially, Banda was born on May 18, 1906. But he is widely believed to have been born before the turn of the century in a village near Kasungu, a trading post in Nyasaland, the name of Malawi before independence.
In the letter Banda urged his party to unite and allow the new generation of politicians to fuse with the veterans.
"Young men and women of sound education with genuine commitment to the party must work side by side with veterans of the Malawi Congress Party. You need new skills in the party to make it dynamic."
On his relationship with the Muluzi government, Banda bemoaned his 1994 election loss and the harassment he has suffered.
He said that although he accepted defeat honourably and did not undermine the present government's authority, it continued to persecute him and his party.

Banda, well known for his stylish dress of a hat and a three-piece suit, was in 1995 acquitted of charges of plotting to murder four senior politicians after doctors said he could not attend the trial because of his frail health and old age.
In June this year fraud charges were also dropped against him involving more than $9 million from government coffers.
The five-day party convention will elect Banda's successor on Tuesday.
